title: A2a Protocol
motto: MCP is agent-to-tool. A2A (Agent2Agent) is agent-to-agent — an open protocol for letting opaque agents built on different frameworks collaborate. Released by Google in April 2025, donated to the Linux Foundation in June 2025, reaching v1.0 in April 2026 with 150+ supporters including AWS, Cisco, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, and ServiceNow. It absorbed IBM's ACP and added the AP2 payments extension. This lesson walks the Agent Card, Task lifecycle, and the two transport bindings.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: MCP is agent-to-tool. A2A (Agent2Agent) is agent-to-agent — an open protocol for letting opaque agents built on different frameworks collaborate. Released by Google in April 2025, donated to the Linux Foundation in June 2025, reaching v1.0 in April 2026 with 150+ supporters including AWS, Cisco, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, and ServiceNow. It absorbed IBM's ACP and added the AP2 payments extension. This lesson walks the Agent Card, Task lifecycle, and the two transport bindings.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A customer-service agent needs to delegate report-writing to a specialized writer agent. Options pre-A2A:

- Custom REST API. Works but every pairing is a one-off.
- Shared codebase. Requires the two agents to run the same framework.
- MCP. Doesn't fit: MCP is for calling tools, not for two agents collaborating while preserving each agent's opaque internal reasoning.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Agent-to-Agent protocol for interoperable multi-vendor agents.
